title: PRD: Service Degradation Controller — automated fallbacks, traffic curators, and verification harness
creator: Asha Patel
description: Translate recent retrospective action items into a scoped PRD that defines a Service Degradation Controller (SDC): a runtime-configurable component that enforces deterministic fallback behavior under resource pressure (throttling, kernel regressions, or regional capacity loss), provides traffic shepherding to reduce blast radius, and exposes a synthetic verification harness for acceptance testing and post-deploy checks.
background: A Feb production disruption exposed gaps in how we degrade: automated fallbacks triggered, but without standardized contract guarantees we saw inconsistent routing, large quality regressions for high-value customers, and gaps in operator verification. Retrospective action items recommended: codify fallback contracts, add traffic shepherding rules to limit blast radius during cache/coldstart storms, and require synthetic acceptance tests executed by the control plane before an SLO-impacting rollout is allowed.
requirements:
1) Define a machine-readable fallback contract schema that maps SLO triggers to ordered mitigation actions (e.g., model-variant swap -> cache-prime -> route-to-dedicated) and a configurable timeout/rollback policy.
2) Implement an SDC API to accept contracts per-deployment and expose active state via Console + traces.
3) Traffic shepherding primitives to reduce concurrent new requests for affected model routes (rate-limits, admission-control, warm-pool drain).
4) Synthetic verification harness: a suite of churn-resistant checks (latency p50/p95, token-cost delta, sample-response quality checks) runnable pre-rollout and as a periodic health job.
5) Operator runbook and observable dashboards for SDC decisions (why a fallback fired, which rule matched, and telemetry linking to traces and KV-cache metrics).
acceptance_criteria:
- Fallback contract schema approved by PM + Runtime + SRE and committed to repo.
- SDC can be deployed in staging and accepts per-deployment contracts via API; Console shows active contract and last-fired rule.
- When a synthetic SLO threshold is crossed in staging, SDC triggers configured ordered mitigation and logs step-by-step decision trace.
- Traffic shepherding primitives can limit new inbound requests for a route by configurable percentages and duration; we validate via synthetic load test showing reduced error budget burn.
- Synthetic verification harness runs as a pre-rollout gate: failures block rollout with explicit failure reasons surfaced to Console.
- Operator runbook drafted with playbook steps and post-fallback verification checklist; at least two SREs have run the checklist in a dry-run.
- Unit/integration tests + e2e validation in our CI with >=90% deterministic pass rate on non-flaky checks.
design_notes: We will prefer a declarative contract format (YAML/JSON) that maps monitored signals (tail-latency, KV-cache-stall-rate, error-rate, queue-length) to an ordered list of mitigation steps. Each mitigation step must be idempotent and have a compensating action (e.g., unban, rollback). To minimize runtime load, SDC will subscribe to aggregated signals from metrics backend instead of polling per-request. We will reuse the existing rollout API surface to attach a contract to a deployment object.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement minimal SDC with contract schema + Console UI visibility and synthetic harness. Phase 2 (canary): attach contracts to 10% of new deployments for low-risk routes; monitor for false positives. Phase 3 (wider rollout): enable traffic shepherding and mandatory pre-rollout verification for all runtime-1.x rollouts on hosted tier. Final: opt-in for Dedicated customers, configurable via tenant settings.
tasks: Draft fallback contract schema and have design review (PM, Runtime, SRE)
Build SDC API and minimal engine to evaluate contracts against aggregated signals
Console: display active contract, history of fired rules, and links to traces
Implement traffic shepherding primitives (rate-limit, admission control hooks)
Create synthetic verification harness and author canonical checks for latency/cost/quality
Author operator runbook and conduct two dry-run exercises with SRE team
Write unit/integration tests and CI e2e job for synthetic verification
Add telemetry and dashboards; correlate SDC actions with KV-cache/queue metrics
